To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BODIPYL-based D–A– D triads have been designed, synthesized, and characterized.

the D–D–A–A–D–D and D–D–D–A molecular systems were designed and synthesized, the optical, electrochemical properties and the charge carrier mobilities were investigated and the surface morphology of these molecular systems were studied.
the D–D–A triads exhibit broader absorption, raising HOMO levels and increasing hole carrier mobilities, which is a promising candidate for OFET applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of D–A– D triads, which can be used as active materials for organic field-effect transistors.
the design, synthesis and characterization of new D–A–A and D–A molecular systems.
a new class of D–A– D triads and D– A dyads containing BODIPY and carbazole, which can be used as active layer in organic field effect transistors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BODIPY based D–A–A–D molecular systems can be considered as promising materials for organic electronic devices.
the introduction of BODIPY into the triphenylamine based D–A– D triads is a good approach to improve hole carrier mobilities and the device performance.
the D–D–A triads are promising for organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) with high charge mobility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BODIPY dyad and triad containing carbazole exhibited high hole mobility, which can be used for the development of organic electronic devices.
the BODIPY-based molecular system could be promising for organic electronic applications.
the introduction of BODIPY into carbazole and triphenylamine could be a good strategy to enhance the hole carrier mobility and the optical properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BODIPY based triads can be used as a new type of hole transporting materials in organic electronic devices.
the incorporation of BODIPY in triphenylamine-based donor–acceptor–donor triads is a promising strategy to design new organic semiconductors.
the incorporation of BODIPY into D–A dyad and D–A-D triad systems can be an effective way to improve charge transport properties of organic semiconductors.
